answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x and isolated to the primary region during peak settlement, so the first move should keep accepting customer writes rather than shed them. Regional failover matches that constraint and the region-scoped symptom; a guarded slice first avoids betting the full settlement peak on an unverified March analogy. Rollback remains plausible because a release shipped two hours ago, which is why b1 should be checked in parallel—but a fleet-wide bad build would not by itself explain primary-only degradation. Circuit breaking and read-replica routing are the wrong tools here (fail-open writes vs. report-read offload). Capacity add is unproven until region health is tested. Settlement-window failover can still disturb downstream posting, so that risk stays flagged and cause attribution stays open.
